feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: India's prime minister is wooing the GenZ while cracking down on them
entry.summary: Over two months, protesters, most who appeared to be digitally-savvy GenZ, used social media to organize. Government's efforts to respond spotlight how the ruling party appears to be playing catch-up.

entry.title: ICE says it now has enough body cameras. And, Congress averts shutdown before midterms
entry.summary: Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it now has enough body cameras to equip all of its agents. And, Congress votes to fund the government, averting a government shutdown ahead of the midterms.

entry.title: Israel bars U.S. citizens over criticism and ties to Palestinian activists, lawyers say
entry.summary: Travelers from the U.S. and other nations are denied entry to Israel after interrogations about their links to Palestinians, plans to visit the occupied West Bank and opinions of Israel, lawyers say.

entry.title: Germany blames Russia for last month's attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport
entry.summary: The German government blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig airport last month using a drone laden with explosives. It announced that it would shut down a Russian consulate among measures.

entry.title: Putin signals support for Iran in ongoing war with the U.S.
entry.summary: Russia's Vladimir Putin is signaling unwavering support for Iran, as Tehran thanks Moscow for backing amid the escalating Middle East war.

entry.title: U.S. military strikes Iran, while Trump vows more for Tehran's retaliation
entry.summary: The U.S. military hit targets in Iran on Tuesday and Tehran fired missiles and drones at various sites across the region in response as hostilities flare once again in an intermittent war.

entry.title: A week after the deadly floods in Nepal, rescuers work to find survivors
entry.summary: Nearly a week after flash floods devastated parts of Nepal and Tibet, rescuers are still searching for people trapped in hydropower plants. But first they have to find the plants.

entry.title: SCOTUS allows Trump's ballroom project to continue. And, the Army secretary resigns
entry.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that President Trump's ballroom project may continue. And, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns after 18 months on the job.

entry.title: Global finance ministers gather in North Carolina for G20 summit
entry.summary: The U.S. is playing host to finance ministers from around the world this week. Russia's top economic official made a stir on Monday when he showed up in person at the meeting in North Carolina.

entry.title: The U.S. wants others to join its economic pressure campaign against Iran. Will they?
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel asks former Deputy National Security Adviser Jon Finer about U.S. efforts to cultivate global support to economically isolate and pressure Iran.
